# Diagnostics: Electrical faults on steering column stalks

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Locate five Phillips head screws in the lower cover on the steering column. [t1684]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Locate the five Phillips head screws in the lower cover on the steering column.
2. Remove all five Phillips head screws from the lower cover.
3. Lift the top cover away from the bottom cover, taking care not to break the clips holding them together.
4. Disconnect the wiring harnesses connecting to the base of the headlight stalk.
5. [Partial] Find and take out the pair of tiny Phillips screws holding the headlight lever on the left steering column.
6. Slide the old headlight stalk straight out to the left.

_Procedure reported by [t1684]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-change-headlight-stalk.3842/>_

## Tools

- [Partial] Phillips head screwdriver [t1684]

## Tips & gotchas

- If switching from a fog-equipped stalk to a plain one, cover the exposed small wiring harness with a nylon cap or electrical tape. [t1684]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Breaking the clips holding the two steering column covers together during removal. [t1684]
